name: Victorian (1890)
note: Steam drainage pumps and hand pumps; no counterflooding system (the sea valves are for the magazines); bulkheads never air-tested, many pipes and cables through them [EST].

name: Pre-dreadnought (1905)
note: Main drainage with steam ejectors; Makarov's and Krylov's counterflooding tables, a few tanks flooded by hand valves (Orel, Retvizan) [EST].

name: RN Great War (1914)
note: Main drainage on the dynamos; counterflooding by hand at the valves, little organised for it (no unified damage control until 1943) [EST].

name: German Great War (1914)
note: Close subdivision, good closure discipline and systematic counterflooding (Seydlitz, Lützow trimmed by it) [EST].

name: Interwar (1939)
note: Electric drainage, submersibles; remote counterflood valves (North Carolina: ~80 t/min on 45,000 t) [EST from WDR 61].

name: USN 1943
note: Wartime lessons: handy-billies (14 t/h) and P-500s (115 t/h) standard, emergency diesels, air-tested compartments (09 §5.2) [EST].
